title: Bending into a different medium
hook: Change second medium refractive index and predict sine of the transmitted angle.
misconception: sine of the transmitted angle doubles when second medium refractive index doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply sinθ₂ = n₁ sinθ₁/n₂ to compare sine of the transmitted angle when second medium refractive index changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed incident angle and first-medium index in a case where transmission occurs, sinθ₂ = n₁ sinθ₁/n₂. When second medium refractive index doubles, sine of the transmitted angle becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model sinθ₂ = n₁ sinθ₁/n₂; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed incident angle and first-medium index in a case where transmission occurs, with a nonzero initial result. If second medium refractive index triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on sine of the transmitted angle?
recall.why: Apply sinθ₂ = n₁ sinθ₁/n₂ under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
